acceptance: With available memory patched to 1.0 GB, check_sufficient_memory for TPC-H SF 0.01 on polars-df passes for a full run, for queries=['6'], and with generation_required=True and the default generator settings.
generation_estimate used for a TPC-H benchmark built with default settings equals (0.1 + 0.30 x 1) x 1.1 GB; with parallel=8 it equals (0.1 + 0.30 x 8) x 1.1 GB (unit tests for both).
For TPC-H SF 0.01 the subset estimate is not larger than the full-run estimate (unit test).

Query-execution estimates for TPC-H SF 1, 10 and 100 (full run and subset) are equal to or larger than before (unit test pinning the pre-change values). Generation estimates use the configured worker count: with os.cpu_count patched to 10, the test states the expected SF 1 generation estimate for parallel=1 and parallel=8.
The measured Polars idle memory (three runs and the median) and the chosen option are recorded in this item's context before the PR opens.
A run refused before the change for a real shortage (for example SF 100 with 4 GB available) is still refused with the same scope wording.
context: Found 2026-11-24 while diagnosing preflight failures on the remove-deprecated-spellings branch. Host: 10 cores, 16 GB, 4.8 GB free after a preflight.
description:
## Problem
The DataFrame memory guard (`check_sufficient_memory` in benchbox/core/dataframe/capabilities.py, called from benchbox/platforms/dataframe/benchmark_mixin.py and benchbox/core/runner/runner.py::_dataframe_generation_guard) refuses tiny runs on a busy host because two parts of its estimate ignore the run:
1. **Generator processes (defect).** `refuse_insufficient_generation_memory` reads `benchmark.parallel` through `_generator_workers`. The `TPCH` object passed in has no `parallel` attribute (the setting lives on `TPCH(...)._impl.parallel`, default 1), so the guard falls back to `os.cpu_count()`. On a 10-core host it estimates (0.1 + 0.30 x 10) x 1.1 = 3.41 GB for generation (4.09 GB with the 20% margin) when the real generator runs one process (about 0.44 GB).
2. **Polars allowance only on the subset path (inconsistency).** `estimate_memory_required` applies `max(modeled, PLATFORM_BASELINE_GB['polars']=2.0)` only when a query subset is selected. TPC-H SF 0.01 estimates 0.02 GB for a full run but 2.0 GB for `--queries 6`, so asking for one query needs about 100 times the memory of asking for all of them.

Observed effect: `--queries 6` at SF 0.01 is refused with InsufficientMemoryError when about 4 GB is free; integration tests that run a small Polars benchmark through MCP fail during busy preflights (see tests-depend-on-host-free-memory-20261124).

## Decision gate
Before changing the Polars allowance, measure the resident memory of an idle Polars process that has loaded TPC-H SF 0.01 Q6 on this host (three runs, report the median). Then choose: (a) apply the measured allowance to both the full-run and subset paths, or (b) remove the allowance from the subset path. Default without owner input: (a) when the measured median is under 0.8 GB (so the value plus the 20% safety margin fits the 1.0 GB acceptance check), using the measured value; if the median is 0.8 GB or more, stop and bring the measurements to the owner. Do not change GENERATION_GB_PER_WORKER, GENERATION_BASE_GB or GENERATION_ESTIMATE_MARGIN without new generator measurements recorded on this item.

## Change
- Read the worker count from the object that owns it (the benchmark implementation the generator uses), falling back to os.cpu_count() only when no setting exists. Cover TPC-H and TPC-DS.
- Make the Polars allowance consistent between the full-run and subset paths per the decision gate.
- Scope: PLATFORM_BASELINE_GB also holds datafusion (2.0 GB) and pyspark (4.0 GB), and the subset path applies only when SF <= SUBSET_MODEL_MAX_SF (10). Apply the same rule to those platforms, or list them as out of scope in the PR with the reason.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create), never the primary clone; heavy test runs only through lock-taking entry points; never set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK or force admission; stage explicit paths; add a changelog.d fragment if users can see the change; no explanatory comments (make comment-policy-check). Do not lower the query-execution estimate for scale factor 1 or above (the generation estimate may fall to the configured worker count), do not make ignore_memory_warnings a default anywhere, and keep the refusal message text naming the scope (data generation or query execution).
